claim: lever_receipts.fire() sits in branches the real train_cpt step loop reaches
why_needed: The module was unit-proven, but unit tests cannot show that the fire() calls are inside the branches that actually execute. Reading the code is what shipped an unloadable checkpoint format earlier in this campaign.
method: Two 2-step CPT runs, identical config and corpus, GPU 1, evalgate oom-shield, CUDA 13.3. The only difference is the fact_ids column, removed for the red arm.

green.note: 32 fires = 2 optimizer steps x 16 grad-accum microbatches

red.loader_line: [lever4] exposure_tracking enabled but corpus has no fact_ids column
red.note: The loader WARNED AND CONTINUED, which is the pre-existing silent-inert path: before receipts this run would have completed reporting lever4 as an active intervention. The audit failed it instead.

ordering_verified: The red arm's checkpoint is on disk with weights intact and its run_contract carries status FAIL / fired 0, so a silent lever kills the run without discarding trained weights and the artifact explains itself.
incidental_defect_found: Both arms first died on CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.8, a debug-tools-only toolkit with no compiler; fixed at the default by scripts/cuda_home.py rather than in this script.
